evidence.source: 說文解字 (Shuowen.org transcription), with Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.field: 姐 entry; graphic analysis and regional sense
evidence.text: The entry says that in Shu (蜀) people called a mother 姐 and in Huainan they called her 社; it analyzes 姐 as 女 semantic element plus 且 phonetic element. Duan comments that 社 and 姐 are close in sound. This is evidence for an old maternal noun and the construction of 姐, but it does not establish that 她’s 也 is a sound component in that old graph.
evidence.title: 說文解字「姐」

evidence.source: Chinese Text Project, Kangxi Dictionary search result
evidence.text: The indexed entry reports 《玉篇》’s gloss that 她 is an old form of 姐. The page itself returned 403 when opened, so this is search-result text rather than inspected page content; it supports only a tentative report of the historical relation.
evidence.title: 她 - 中國哲學書電子化計劃

evidence.source: 畢新偉, 《「她」字的來源與女性主體性》, 21世紀雙月刊
evidence.field: historical discussion of 她 and 姐; 玉篇 and 六書故 references
evidence.text: The article reports that 她 occurs in the Liang-period 玉篇 as an old form of 姐, and cites 元代戴侗《六書故》 for the account that 姐’s old form may be written 她, with 也 as phonetic element. It gives 姐 and 她 readings from later rhyme dictionaries as jie-like (集韻 子野切 for 她). This is a secondary scholarly discussion, not a direct inspection of those historical dictionaries; it indicates a historical noun/name relation and a possible 也 phonetic analysis, but does not show the old glyph or establish a pronunciation for any depicted referent.
evidence.title: 「她」字的來源與女性主體性

evidence.source: 中国作家网 article on 她
evidence.text: The article reports a dated modern reuse: Zhou Zuoren’s preface to his translation 《改革》 in 《新青年》 5.2, dated 1918-08-15, records Liu Bannong’s proposal to use 她 alongside 他. It distinguishes the old graph, reported from 玉篇 with mother-related senses, from the modern feminine third-person pronoun meaning. It reports broad uptake around 1921 and a 1924 decision defining 她 as the feminine third-person pronoun, then proposing the reading yi, distinct from 他’s ta. The article’s account supports semantic reuse and later reading standardization, not an uninterrupted semantic history from the old maternal noun to the pronoun.
evidence.title: “她”自何处来

evidence.field: A00906-001, research note and variant explanation
evidence.text: The Ministry of Education identifies 她 as a historical variant of 姐, with historical reading jiě and later pronoun reading tā. It cites the Ji Yun: 姐, 她, and 媎 are listed together; the entry says 姐’s old form included another graph, with 她 and 媎 as alternatives. This supports the historical 姐 relationship but does not establish a continuous semantic path to the modern feminine pronoun.
evidence.title: [A00906-001] 她 (姐) - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Chinese Text Project, Kangxi Dictionary entry
evidence.text: The indexed entry quotes the Kangxi Dictionary’s reports: the Yu Pian calls 她 an old form of 姐; the Shuowen account says Shu called a mother 姐 and Huainan called her 社; and the Liu Shu Gu says 姐 could be written 她 with 也 as phonetic, or 媎 with 者 as phonetic. This is an inspected web search result, not an opened primary dictionary page.
evidence.title: 她 - 中國哲學書電子化計劃

evidence.text: The article reports early twentieth-century use of 她 as a feminine third-person pronoun, including the 1919 article 《她为什么死？》, Liu Bannong’s 1920 published argument for the form, increased uptake in 1921, and a 1924 education-group resolution defining 她 as the feminine third-person pronoun and assigning it the reading yi. These reports document modern semantic reuse and changing proposals for its reading; they do not establish an uninterrupted semantic history from the older mother-related noun.
evidence.title: “她”自何处来

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: No directly inspected paleographic image or manuscript/printed 玉篇 witness for the early 她 form; the report of its old-form relationship comes from secondary discussion and an inaccessible Ctext result.

The exact earliest attestation of 她 and its local/dialectal sense distribution remain unverified. The sources inspected distinguish the old maternal noun from the modern pronoun but do not document a continuous semantic pathway.
The cited account of 她 as 姐’s old form and 也 as a phonetic element is a secondary report. A direct primary dictionary page for 六書故 or the relevant 玉篇 passage was not inspected.

No independently supported phonetic etymology establishes an ancient sound relation of 也 to an object or source word depicted by that graph. This is not a whole-graph phonetic-loan claim; available evidence only suggests 也 may be a sound element in the historical 姐/她 orthographic alternative.

The local Unihan rows show 她 tā and 也 yě; Unihan records modern readings only. Official Unicode per-character records were inaccessible, so no external Unihan click-through claim is made. The local Baxter–Sagart dataset has an entry for 也 (*lAjʔ) but none for 她; same-system historical comparison for the host is therefore unavailable.

Sources disagree in emphasis about the modern pronoun’s origin: accounts describe European-language translation pressure, local modern linguistic/social needs, and reuse of an old graph. Evidence supports a 1918 proposal and later adoption, but does not settle a single-cause explanation.

No oracle-bone, bronze, manuscript or early printed witness of 她 was inspected. The older form relationship is supported through later dictionary reports and the Ministry of Education’s account, not direct paleographic evidence.

The old sense reported for the 她/姐 relationship concerns a mother or female kin term, but exact earliest attestation and regional distribution were not independently verified from the cited primary witnesses.

The suggested 女 semantic element plus 也 phonetic element is reported for an alternative old spelling of 姐 in the Liu Shu Gu. It does not prove that 她 was originally formed as an independent 女+也 compound, and no ancient sound comparison for 姐 and 也 was established here.
Modern tā and yě are not evidence of historical phonetic compatibility. Local Baxter–Sagart data provides 也 as MC yaeX, OC *lAjʔ but no 她 entry; a same-system host comparison is unavailable.
The Unicode per-character lookup pages for U+5979 and U+4E5F could not be opened, so the repository readings cannot be externally verified through the required official character-specific links.

The modern pronoun’s motivations are presented in differing accounts as translation needs, writing practice and social-linguistic reform. The inspected material documents dated use and debate but does not settle a single cause.

The Commons seal-script image is a modern redraw sourced to Chinese Etymology data; it illustrates the claimed component shape, not an ancient 她 artifact. No suitable image of an early 她 witness was established.

limitations.text: No historical glyph image of 她 is shown. The available image depicts 也 in a modern seal-script-style redraw; that shape alone cannot establish 她’s earliest form or its historical relationship to 姐. Later dictionary reports identify 她 as an old form of 姐 and report 也 as a phonetic element in an alternative spelling, but no early 她 witness is available to illustrate that account.
